newsitem.title: GREECE: ELECTIONS SIGNAL A NEW ERA, NOT PROBLEM SOLVING-ANDRIANOPOULOS.
newsitem.headline: ELECTIONS SIGNAL A NEW ERA, NOT PROBLEM SOLVING-ANDRIANOPOULOS.

text.p: The upcoming Greek elections will herald the start of a new era but will not solve any problems, former conservative industry minister Andreas Andrianopoulos told Sky TV station in an interview.

"These elections will not solve problems. They are just the beginning of a new era," said Andrianopoulos adding that there were no easy solutions and that Greece had to go through a painful period of adjustment.
Asked if he was contemplating setting up a liberal political party, Andrianopoulos declined to give a clear answer.

He said public information was controlled by a few people who relie on state procurements. They would not loosen their grip on the media for fear of losing their political influence and in turn state contracts.

"Information is controlled in Greece," he said. "Hopefully, Greeks will soon discover that the policies espoused by the parties are leading to a stalemate and they will decide to try something different."
He said future economic growth would come from investments in new technologies but this required an educated work force which was not currently available in Greece as the 1991 census showed.
Investments in the agricultural sector and the heavy industry would not bring about the expected economic development, he said.
Asked if extended privatisations could solve Greece's problems, Andrianopoulos said privatisations should have taken place years ago when there was demand and buyers.
"In Greece, we are dealing with issues that have been resolved a decade ago in the Western world. It is always like that," said Andrianopoulos.

Commenting on Greek-Turkish relations, he said the role of Turkey in connection with the petroleum reserves in the Caspian Sea and former Islamic republics of the Soviet Union and what that meant for Greece had not been discussed in the pre-election period.
"I find it disappointing," he said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
